title: Timeout & Context Deadline Propagation
subtitle: End-to-end SLA time budgeting, context deadline propagation via gRPC metadata, and immediate thread reclamation.
keyTakeaways: Every network call must have an explicit timeout; default infinite socket timeouts are a ticking time bomb in production.
Implement **Deadline Propagation**: calculate an end-to-end SLA budget (e.g. 2000ms) at ingress and propagate the remaining time budget downstream.
When an upstream request times out, downstream operations must detect the expired deadline and immediately cancel in-flight queries.
architectureDiagram:
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                  DEADLINE BUDGET PROPAGATION PIPELINE                   |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
[Edge Client: SLA 2000ms]
       |  (Header: X-Request-Deadline: now + 2000ms)
       v
[API Gateway: Consumes 200ms -> Remaining Budget: 1800ms]
       |  (Header: X-Request-Deadline: remaining 1800ms)
       v
[Order Svc: Consumes 600ms -> Remaining Budget: 1200ms]
       |  (Header: X-Request-Deadline: remaining 1200ms)
       v
[Payment Svc: Hangs for 1300ms! Context CANCELED at 1200ms mark!]
       (Immediate Thread Reclaim; Returns 504 Gateway Timeout)

sections.heading: Why Independent Timeouts Fail Without Deadlines
sections.body: If Service A has a timeout of 5s, Service B has a timeout of 5s, and Service C has a timeout of 5s, an edge call can hang for 15 seconds before failing! Even worse: if Service A times out after 5s and returns an error to the user, Service B and C may continue executing for another 10 seconds, burning expensive database and CPU resources for a client that has already closed their browser. In gRPC and Go, `context.WithDeadline` automatically cancels child contexts when the deadline expires.
bullets: gRPC Deadline: Natively transmitted in HTTP/2 headers as `grpc-timeout`.
Database Query Cancellation: When a context is cancelled, PostgreSQL triggers `STATEMENT_TIMEOUT` to cancel in-flight queries.
Wasted Work Elimination: Never compute results for a client that has already aborted the HTTP connection.

tradeOffs.pros: Strict SLA enforcement across multi-hop calls, eliminates wasted server work, prevents cascading hangs.
tradeOffs.cons: Requires passing context or headers across every RPC and database driver.
tradeOffs.bestFor: All microservices; standard in gRPC and modern Go/Java architectures.

tradeOffs.pros: Simple to configure on individual HTTP clients.
tradeOffs.cons: Cumulative latency stacks up; downstream services waste CPU computing abandoned results.

interviewTip: Explain: 'I will implement Deadline Propagation using gRPC metadata. The API gateway sets a 2-second deadline; each microservice subtracts its own processing time. If the deadline expires, all downstream operations are cancelled immediately to eliminate wasted work.'
